issues.description: validate_conda substring match on --version output accepts impostor binaries.
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` admits any binary whose --version output contains 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' as a substring (e.g. 'anaconda-uninstall', 'conda-build', or unrelated tools printing those paths). Match on the leading token or basename, or parse a known version format, so the postcondition 'this is conda/mamba/micromamba' actually holds.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the browse dialog breaks Linux and macOS users.
issues.detail: Conda, mamba, and micromamba on POSIX systems are extensionless binaries, so a hardcoded '*.exe' filter leaks a Windows-only assumption through a cross-platform abstraction and shows an empty file picker on Linux/macOS. Make the filter platform-conditional, drop it, or fall back to 'All files'.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for an empty path, lying about validity.
issues.detail: Returning True for '' conflates 'no input supplied' with 'valid executable' and breaks the function's contract that True implies a usable conda binary. Downstream callers can't trust the result. Either return False and let the UI layer decide that empty means 'unset', or split the contract into is_empty vs is_valid.

issues.description: validate_conda spawns a subprocess on every keystroke, blocking the UI.
issues.detail: If wired to textChanged, each edit spawns conda/mamba --version, which can take hundreds of ms. Debounce or only validate on editingFinished/focus-out. Torvalds also notes the Popen object is discarded without checking returncode, which risks leaking pipes across a session of live validation.

issues.description: kernelspec argv() trusts the persisted custom conda_path without re-validation.
issues.detail: When custom_conda is True, conda_path is read and used directly; only a falsy value triggers the error path. A stale or broken persisted path bypasses validation at use-time. Re-check with validate_conda on use and surface a precise error pointing at the preference, and consider routing the cross-plugin read through a named accessor to hide the section string.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to shared create_browsefile helper affects every caller.
issues.detail: create_browsefile is shared infrastructure used by many preference pages. Adding edit.setFocus() after select_file changes focus behavior for every caller, not just the conda case. Move the focus call into the conda caller, and document the new validate_callback/validate_reason contract on the helper.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-scoped patch that ships with sloppy validation. validate_conda uses a loose substring match on --version output, returns True for empty input, and runs an expensive subprocess that can fire on every keystroke. A hardcoded '*.exe' file filter breaks Linux/macOS users by leaking a Windows assumption through a cross-platform abstraction. Secondary issues: kernelspec trusts the persisted path without re-validation, and a setFocus side effect was added to a shared widget helper. Needs-work, not a blocker — tighten the validator, fix the filter, and move the focus call to the caller.
